Commentary.Commentary: Right then, this highly anticipated five-match T20I series has been sealed by India Women 3-1 but there's still a game to go and neither side would want to end the series with a defeat, especially with an ODI series to follow after that. The fifth and final T20I will be played on Saturday, 12 June in Birmingham. The game will begin at 11.05 pm IST (5.35 pm GMT), but you can join us a lot sooner for the build-up. Until next time then. Cheers!

The Indian captain, Harmanpreet Kaur, is up for a chat now. She says they feel really grateful that they won the series. Adds that it was important for them to get the momentum. Shares that they had very good camps back home before coming to the UK. Points about executing the plans well and everyone playing according to their roles. Also shares that they have now played three seasons of WPL and every season has been special for them, which has provided valuable experience to execute in international cricket. Ends by saying that they just want to keep doing the right things repeatedly.

England Women skipper, Tammy Beaumont,  says that a couple of contrasting games and probably 150 was needed on this track, and they simply didn't get things right. Adds that they need to be better with the bat and holds her hand up regarding her soft dismissal, but also gives credit to India and says they bowled and fielded well. Mentions that India assessed conditions quickly and took the pace off the ball, and with a bit of pressure off the shoulders, they want to put in a complete performance in the final game.

Radha Yadav is named Player of the Match for her stellar bowling performance. She says the team is charged up from the outset of the series and credits their preparation and focus on fine details, like spinning the ball with more intent and executing yorkers precisely, for the results showing on the field. On adapting to conditions different from The Oval, Radha notes that it feels more natural here, as the surface suits their bowling style and feels familiar, helping them settle in quickly. Highlights that all bowlers did really well and they are looking forward to the next game. On the fielding efforts, she mentions that this is the part that they were trying to get better and says they did well in that department too.
The Presentation ceremony...

Earlier in the game, Tammy Beaumont won the toss and just like the last game, she elected to bat first on a pitch that was very much on the slower side. The Indian bowlers were quick to take pace off the ball and saw the back of the English openers, who made a half century each in the previous game. From there on, it was all about keeping the pressure on the batters and the bowlers created opportunities with the fielders backing them up by holding onto the catches. Radha Yadav, in particular, was impressive and picked up a couple of wickets, and so did young sensation Shree Charani. England Women didn't have any batter even go past the 25-run mark and the lack of partnerships meant that they only mustered up 126 runs, thanks to a flourish in the final over from Issy Wong and Sophie Ecclestone.

With just 10 needed for the win, Harmanpreet fell and soon, Amanjot Kaur followed but with plenty of balls left, Richa Ghosh and Jemimah Rodrigues finished things up in a hurry and India sealed the game with 3 overs remaining. A historic moment indeed and they will now be eyeing to pile on more misery on the hosts in the final game.

The innings slowed down in the middle overs as England managed to pick up a couple of wickets and used the sluggishness of the track to their advantage. The likes of Sophie Ecclestone and Issy Wong used the variations nicely and Charlie Dean and Lauren Filer bowled with a lot of heart. However, India Women were always just one decent stand away from victory and that came when skipper Harmanpreet Kaur and Jemimah Rodrigues stitched together 48 runs. The boundaries didn't flow in that stand as the hosts built up pressure with a lot of dot balls but the duo managed to break free towards the end.

127 runs needed for the win and it seemed pretty straightforward at the break. However, 121 has been the average score here in recent times but the way the Indian openers started, it definitely did look like a pitch where you needed a score of around 150. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma picked up 53 runs in the Powerplay and broke the back of the run chase and it seemed like the English had no answer to the carnage.

HISTORY HAS BEEN MADE AT OLD TRAFFORD! India Women have their maiden T20I series win against England Women and they have sealed the five-match series with a game in hand. A terrific showing from the Women in Blue and they have deserved it. England, on the other hand, will be disappointed but this is a team that is in transition and they will be looking to bounce back in the final game.

THAT'S IT! That's the moment! History has been created at Manchester as India Women register their first T20I series win on English soil. Rodrigues shuffles across the line and paddles it very fine to the fence at deep fine leg. INDIA WIN BY 6 WICKETS AND 18 BALLS TO SPARE!

Commentary.Commentary: Tosses this one up around off, Mandhana leans on and strokes it towards mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Sophie Ecclestone to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Just picking the gaps here, Mandhana! Into the pitch and on the stumps, Mandhana swivels onto the back foot and turns it away through the leg side, to the left of deep mid-wicket and finds the boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Sophie Ecclestone to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On the shorter side around middle, tucked away towards mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Sophie Ecclestone to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sophie Ecclestone is brought into the attack now. She replaces Charlie Dean.

FOUR! That's brilliant! Full and angled into the pads, Shafali Verma flicks it away off the legs and whips it wide of mid on, over the infield and into the fence. 14 off the over and 39 off the last 3 overs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Lauren Bell to Shafali Verma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Good length around the top of off, Verma backs away to play at it but is well beaten. Good bowling!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Lauren Bell to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Quick hands from Shafali Verma. Full and trying to follow the batter down leg, but Verma adjusts and stays put before clobbering it back over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Lauren Bell to Shafali Verma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: NO BALL! Oh, deary me! That has gone all wrong for Lauren Bell. An attempted slower ball that slips out of the hands and ends up being a beamer. Shafali Verma ducks as the ball goes over her and the stumps. Free Hit coming up...
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Lauren Bell to Shafali Verma, No ball!

Commentary.Commentary: Very full and outside off, Mandhana leans across and caresses it on the full, through cover-point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Lauren Bell to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and outside off again, driven away along the turf and straight to extra cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Lauren Bell to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Oh, that's class! Full and wide, a low full toss, but Mandhana just takes a step to the off side, opens the bat face and glides it through backward point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Lauren Bell to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and angled across off, Verma backs away and gets under the ball before lofting it up and over the cover region for a couple of runs more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Charlie Dean to Shafali Verma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! It's carnage out there from the Indian openers! Fired in a bit on off and middle, Shafali Verma gets leg side of the ball and down on one knee before swatting it back over the bowler's head for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Charlie Dean to Shafali Verma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter delivery on off, Mandhana pushes it out towards extra cover and the batters scamper through for the single. The bowler herself chases after the ball and hears a loud call from Amy Jones to throw it to the keeper. Dean does that and Jones whips off the bails but Verma is well in. The umpires go upstairs to have a look but the very first replay confirms that Verma is safe.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Charlie Dean to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A tad shorter and angled into the pads, Mandhana fails to get it away and gets hit on the pads. A stifled appeal from the bowler and nothing more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Charlie Dean to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Fine shot! Tossed up, full and on off, Smriti Mandhana clears the front leg and effortlessly swings it away wide of long on for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Charlie Dean to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Quick and flat, around off, Mandhana punches it straight to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Charlie Dean to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Spin has been introduced early. Charlie Dean is into the attack now. She replaces Lauren Bell.
Even shorter and banged in outside off, Shafali Verma reaches out and carves the ball away over backward point. This one plugs in the outfield and the fielder is able to chase it down. Two taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Lauren Filer to Shafali Verma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Hammered! Aggressive but predictable from Filer, bowling it short and outside off. Shafali Verma stays put and slaps the ball flat and back over the bowler's head for a third boundary in the over. It seems like Verma's picked up some Wimbledon fever from London.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Lauren Filer to Shafali Verma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A bumper now, wide of the off stump, comes slower off the deck. Verma backs away a bit too much and has to just leave it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Lauren Filer to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Thwarted away by Shafali Verma! Expects the short ball and gets it as well. This is bowled over off, Verma backs away and slaps it in between point and cover-point for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Lauren Filer to Shafali Verma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Good length on off, angling in, Verma backs away again to open up the off side but misses as the ball travels just over the stumps.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Lauren Filer to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Just enough elevation on that one! Shafali Verma expects the short ball and hangs back but this is pitched up at the stumps. Verma stays leg side of the ball and manages to loft it over Issy Wong at mid on for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Lauren Filer to Shafali Verma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Lauren Filer to bowl from the other end.
Hard length around off, Verma stays compact and drops the ball down in front of point for a quick single. 6 runs off the first over of the chase.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Lauren Bell to Shafali Verma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length on off, shaping away, Shafali Verma steps out to hit over covers but ends up dragging it to mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Lauren Bell to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit short and wide, Mandhana extends the arms and flays it away between short third and point and to deep backward point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Lauren Bell to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and around off, Mandhana looks to punch it into the off side but gets it off the inside half of the blade to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Lauren Bell to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Helped 'round the corner and India Women are away! Short of a good length, straying on the pads, Mandhana tickles it down to fine leg and the ball rolls away into the fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Lauren Bell to Smriti Mandhana, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A bit of swing straightaway for Bell! Pitches it on a good length on middle and gets it to shape back into the left-hander. Smriti Mandhana tucks it away to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Lauren Bell to Smriti Mandhana, No run.
